archive.char_locked: You haven’t crossed paths with this character yet.
archive.title: Archive
bio.archivist: She files every name and every door. In a drawer that never opens she keeps the Pianist’s hands.
bio.chair: He founded the house and sat down to wait for the others. The Nurse adjusts his dose so he doesn’t stand “for his own good”.
bio.child: He remembers you better than you remember him. The Cook always keeps a hot plate for him that no one has seen him eat.
bio.concierge: He keeps every key in the house and charges for opening doors. He knows the way out and is in no hurry to tell you: he stayed too.
bio.cook: He cooks with what the house owes and preserves memories in jars. He shares an apron and debts with his brother, the Vendor.
bio.dealer: He has no name. He keeps the ledger and deals a deck of fifty-two cards… and one that is missing.
bio.drowned: He paid his debt with water. The Sister baptized him for too long and now he lives downstairs.
bio.girl: She lies almost every time. The Nurse stitched her left eye shut so she would stop seeing what she shouldn’t; every night she asks her to stitch it again.
bio.merchant: He sells memories in jars. He gets them from his brother, the Cook, who preserves them.
bio.nun: She hears everyone’s confession, even the Dealer’s. She knows his name; a confession is sacred and she will not say it.
bio.nurse: She cares for everyone who stays. She stitched the Girl’s eye and keeps the Man in the Chair seated; neither has thanked her.
bio.pianist: He played for the Dealer when it all began and paid with his hands. He still plays the only piece he remembers.
bio.prompter: He lives in the prompt box below the stage and whispers everyone’s lines. He wrote the script the Dummy repeats… or so he thinks, since he no longer remembers whether he wrote it or merely copied it.
bio.puppet: He speaks with the voice of whoever paid him. He repeats the Dealer’s script word for word… and sometimes one word ahead: the Prompter whispers it from the box.
bio.usher: She knows every seat and who it belongs to. She walks guests to their armchairs and has never seen one leave; she keeps number 13 for you.
bio.watcher: He watches every screen at once and remembers what he saw on each. Only one room is shown by no camera. The Nurse brings him dinner; he never looks up.
bio.woman: She dances in a dress she can no longer take off. The Pianist plays for her and she never asks him to stop.
boss.chair.a: “Sit. Here the blood goes cold and your cards give no heat.”
boss.chair.l: “The chair always wins. It is the only thing I know about it.”
boss.chair.w: “I stand. I have sat so long I forget how it is done.”
boss.child.a: “Do you remember me? I remember you. Don’t close your eyes… oh, they’re already closed.”
boss.child.l: “Again. You always lose here. You always come back.”
boss.child.w: “You beat me. I wanted you to. Now you have to grow up.”
boss.cook.a: “It’s lean times in this kitchen. Put more on the table and don’t complain about the steam.”
boss.cook.l: “No debt, no house. Sit down, it’s getting cold.”
boss.cook.w: “You’ve cleaned your plate. Take something before my brother sells it.”
boss.dealer.a: “The last hand. No stakes, no tricks. Everything in plain sight.”
boss.dealer.l: “It was always my table. Get up; we will start again.”
boss.dealer.w: “Well played. For a moment I thought I would be the one who didn’t get up.”
boss.drowned.a: “Breathe while you can. Every card you play will sink you a little.”
boss.drowned.l: “Drink, drink. It’s only water. It’s only a debt.”
boss.drowned.w: “I already paid. Or so I thought. Go up; nothing is left down here.”
boss.girl.a: “We play the no-repeat game. I notice everything with the eye I can’t see with.”
boss.girl.l: “Again the same thing, again the same thing. You bore me.”
boss.girl.w: “You beat me and you didn’t lie. How strange. Take what you like.”
boss.nun.a: “Confess your hands before you play them. What is repeated is remembered, and what is remembered is paid for.”
boss.nun.l: “Pray, child. The house doesn’t listen, but it takes notes.”
boss.nun.w: “I forgive what you owe me. The Dealer’s is another account. Go on.”
boss.nurse.a: “Breathe deeply, dear. Your eyes won’t do you any good here, and the air is running out.”
boss.nurse.l: “Easy now, it’s just a pinprick. They all say the same and they all go back to bed.”
boss.nurse.w: “You’re cured. How strange; no one ever is here. Leave before I change my mind.”
boss.prompter.a: “You’re in your place. Don’t look at the box; say your line and the rest will follow. And don’t repeat yourself: the audience gets bored.”
boss.prompter.l: “You missed your cue, child. Take it from the top; I’ll tell you when.”
boss.prompter.w: “That’s the show. You improvised, and that wasn’t written. Then… who prompted you?”
boss.title: GUARDIAN
boss.watcher.a: “I see you on twenty-three screens. Don’t try to hide cards or repeat plays: I remember everything.”
boss.watcher.l: “Recorded. Your defeat is already in the archive, with a timestamp. Start again; I’ll record that too.”
boss.watcher.w: “A blind spot… Well. I didn’t know there was one. I’m switching this camera off; go through before anyone sees I wasn’t looking.”

card.hueso_liso.name: Smooth Bone

cookies.title: Cookies and storage

debug.title: Debug
deck.hint: Hover (or tap) a card to see what it does.
deck.title: Deck
dlg.final.1: You have reached the last table. They always get this far.
dlg.final.2: One more hand. I deal. Nobody stakes anything: everything is seen.
dlg.final.3: If you win, we’ll talk about the door. If you lose, you begin again. It’s the same thing, really.
dlg.final.4: Good. One last bullet remains. One more thing and I let you go.
dlg.final.5: Six chambers. Four marks each. This time nobody is watching… except the house.
dlg.final.duel_won: “The game is over. Only the door is left.”
dlg.final.lost: “You lost the last hand. The house collects with interest.”
dlg.final.won: “You won the hand. The house falls silent.”
door.hint: Each ending asks for something different. Choose carefully.
door.req.partida: Requires: “The players” and having met 5 characters.
door.req.verdad: Requires: 5 endings seen and “All the doors are the same”.
door.title: The Door
duel.anomaly: “That was not the bullet I expected.”
duel.contract.honest: It wasn’t lying: Debt rises by 20.
duel.contract.lied: The contract bites: {name} loses a mark.
duel.ev.f_table_backfire: The Table turns on {name}: it loses a mark.
duel.ev.p_table_backfire: The Table sends the bullet back: you lose a mark.
duel.ev.p_table_safe: The Table stays silent. You keep your turn.
duel.h.title: Shot history
duel.heard_loaded: You think you hear… a bullet.
duel.n.backfire_f: The Table sends the bullet back at {name}.
duel.n.backfire_p: The Table sends the bullet back at you.
duel.n.f_aim_p: {name} aims at you and pulls the trigger…
duel.n.p_aim_foe: You aim at {name} and pull the trigger…
duel.n.p_aim_table: You tempt the Table: you rest the barrel on the felt…
duel.n.p_loses: You lose a mark. You have {n} left.
duel.n.pass_p: The turn comes back to you.
duel.n.reload: The shotgun reloads: six new chambers. {name} announces {n} bullets.
duel.n.safe_f: The Table stays silent: {name} keeps the turn.
duel.n.safe_p: The Table stays silent: you keep your turn.
duel.n.skip_hint: Tap the screen to speed up.
duel.setup.note: If you win: +10 extra Money. If you lose: −12 Health on top of the stake. Nobody makes you believe what they announce.
duel.setup.sub: What do you put on the table?
duel.stake.card.name: A card from your deck
duel.stake.debt.name: {n} Debt
duel.stake.money.name: {n} Money
duel.stake.sanity.name: {n} Sanity
duel.title: THE SHOTGUN
duel.tool.memory: The foe will forget its next turn.
egg.arrepentido.hint: Buy and sell without leaving the shop.
egg.arrepentido.name: Buy and Regret
egg.arrepentido.text: You bought a joker and sold it in the same visit. The Vendor sighs: “They always come back.”
egg.ases.hint: Every Ace, in a single play.
egg.ases.name: Four Aces
egg.ases.text: Four Aces in one hand. Nobody deals like that by accident.
egg.cinco.hint: A hand has five fingers; a court, five jokers.
egg.cinco.name: Five Jesters
egg.cinco.text: A whole court of jokers whispers behind you. You’ll have to pay for the party.
egg.colapso.hint: Looking too long at what you shouldn’t.
egg.colapso.name: Zero Sanity
egg.colapso.text: Your mind shattered completely. The house notes it with a smile and gives you just enough to go on.
egg.jackpot.hint: Three lucky numbers together in one hand.
egg.jackpot.name: Triple Seven
egg.jackpot.text: Three sevens in one hand. Bells ring that don’t exist.
egg.konami.hint: A key code from another era, typed on the menu.
egg.konami.name: Ancient Code
egg.konami.text: An old combination from another era. The Dealer pretends not to have seen it.
egg.limite.hint: Win with no margin at all: on the last play.
egg.limite.name: By a Hair
egg.limite.text: You won on your very last play, with the house already smiling.
egg.mesa3.hint: In the duel, tempt the Table and have it not answer… three times in a row.
egg.mesa3.name: The Table Falls Silent
egg.mesa3.text: You tempted the Table three times running and it stayed silent all three. No one had spoken to it like that.
egg.ojos.hint: On the menu, the Dealer’s eyes never leave you. Touch them, again and again.
egg.ojos.name: He Looks Back
egg.ojos.text: Seven times you stared into the Dealer’s eyes. For once, he blinks.
egg.paciencia.hint: The house has all night. Maybe you do too.
egg.paciencia.name: Patience
egg.paciencia.text: You waited a full minute without touching anything. The house appreciates those who can wait; it almost never repays them.
egg.poliglota.name: The House Speaks Every Language
egg.poliglota.text: Spanish, English, French, German and Basque: the debt is understood the same in all five.
egg.real.hint: The noblest hand of the full deck, ten to Ace.
egg.real.name: Royal Flush
egg.real.text: Ten, Jack, Queen, King and Ace of one suit. The Dealer stops shuffling for a second… then shuffles again.
ending.crupier.epi: Someone sits across from you for the first time. You smile without moving your mouth.
ending.crupier.text: You ask him to take off the smile. Beneath it there is no face: only a mirror showing your age. “I won so long ago I forgot how to leave,” he says. He hands you the deck and sits in your chair. Now you are the one who deals.
ending.crupier.title: The Dealer
ending.deuda.epi: The House always wins. But today it took longer.
ending.deuda.text: You play the last hand and win. The House writes the win in its ledger and hands you back a black chip. “You still owe me a game,” it says. You stand. The door stays shut, but now you can count.
ending.deuda.title: The Debt
ending.espectador.epi: Whoever watches is also in the game.
ending.espectador.text: You look out of the room, where nobody should look. Behind the glass there is a face lit by a screen. It is you, or someone watching you play. You study each other for a second. Then the house lowers the curtain.
ending.espectador.title: The Spectator
ending.partida.epi: Without players, the house is just a room with lights.
ending.partida.text: You call them by name, one by one: the girl, the man in the chair, the drowned man, the archivist, the child. Each rises from their table. Nobody remembered being a player. They drop their cards all at once. The game ends because nobody is left who wants to go on.
ending.partida.title: The Game
ending.puerta.epi: The door closes by itself. This time, on the right side.
ending.puerta.text: The bone key turns without a sound. Behind the door is a corridor and, at its end, another identical door. You cross it anyway. Outside there is real air and a sign: CLOSED FOR RENOVATION. For the first time, nobody is watching you.
ending.puerta.title: The Door
ending.true_hint: You have seen five endings. One more door remains.
ending.verdad.epi: Thank you for playing. You can stop watching now.
ending.verdad.text: You have seen every ending. You know all the doors are the same and that the one watching is you. You close the ledger and write the last line. The house goes dark. There is no more game: only the one who played it, and the silence on the other side of the screen.
ending.verdad.title: The Truth
event.archive_ledger.ra: The columns of figures are games. All end at the same door. You understand there aren’t so many doors.
event.archive_ledger.rb: “Wise choice,” she says. “Though it changes nothing.” She gives you a few coins for your discretion.
event.archive_ledger.text: A woman in thick glasses files ledgers that drip ink. “Every name is here,” she says. “And every door is the same.”
event.archive_ledger.title: The Archivist
event.blood_vending.ra: The machine hums, satisfied, and spits out a warm card.
event.blood_vending.rb: The machine powers down with a sigh. For a moment it seemed disappointed.
event.blood_vending.text: A machine dispenses cards for a pinprick on the finger. A sign reads: “No change given.”
event.blood_vending.title: The card machine
event.camera_13.ra: The glass is warm. On the picture, someone turns slowly toward the camera… and looks exactly like you. The screen spits a few coins out of its slot.
event.camera_13.rb: You pull the cable. The picture goes out and, for an instant, the whole room breathes. You look like someone who has just spared himself a fright.
event.camera_13.text: In a corner, a screen shows an empty room with an armchair. On the armchair, your coat. Under the glass, a label: “Camera 13 — live.”
event.camera_13.title: Camera 13
event.chair_bet.ra: He throws the dice without looking. You hear them roll and stop just as you stop listening.
event.chair_bet.rb: “I understand,” he murmurs. “I would rather not get up, either.”
event.chair_bet.text: The Man in the Chair does not stand, and perhaps cannot. “I bet the chair,” he says in a worn voice. “Against your patience.”
event.chair_bet.title: The chair
event.chair_secret.ra: He speaks for hours, or seconds. In the end you understand whose chair it is and why he guards it.
event.chair_secret.rb: He falls silent. The whole house seems to hold its breath until you walk away.
event.chair_secret.text: “This house was founded by a tired player,” says the Man in the Chair. “Who stayed to wait for the others.” The chair creaks.
event.chair_secret.title: The founder
event.chapel_candles.ra: The flame is cold and steady. Something in the chapel sighs. You keep a stub for later.
event.chapel_candles.rb: You blow them out one by one. In the dark the chapel seems larger, and more yours. You find offering coins on the floor.
event.chapel_candles.text: There are candles everywhere and none burns down. Each carries a name written in wax. Yours is unlit.
event.chapel_candles.title: A thousand candles
event.child_1.ra: It nods, satisfied. “Me too.” It hands you a candy that tastes of metal.
event.child_1.rb: “Liar,” it says without malice. Up close its face resembles a childhood photo of you that you never saw.
event.child_1.text: A child in a birthday dress tugs your sleeve. “Did you lose again?” it asks. It isn’t a question.
event.child_1.title: The child
event.child_2.ra: You fold the paper. It is heavy. Somewhere in the house a corridor has turned to make room for a new door.
event.child_2.rb: It shrugs and crosses out the door. A moment later the chalk redraws it by itself.
event.child_2.text: The child draws a door in red chalk and writes a number above it: 13. “It’s in the corridor. It only opens if you know which.”
event.child_2.title: The drawing
event.concierge_1.ra: The room smells of lavender and old paper. You sleep as you haven’t in years. The next morning the Concierge sees you off with a nod: “Come back whenever you like; no one ever leaves.”
event.concierge_1.rb: He smiles without showing his teeth and jingles the ring. “I have a key for every door. Except one.” He stares at an empty hook on the wall. “Someone else has that.”
event.concierge_1.text: A white-haired man with an enormous key ring taps a little bell. “Welcome, Guest. A room for one night: twenty. Here we charge for sleeping, for leaving and for coming in.”
event.concierge_1.title: The front desk
event.concierge_2.ra: The key chills in your hand and turns into a card that wasn’t in the deck. The Concierge doesn’t wake, but his smile twists, like someone dreaming of unpaid bills.
event.concierge_2.rb: You settle his head on his arms. When he wakes he says nothing, but he notes something on your account: one line fewer. “Courtesy of the house,” he murmurs.
event.concierge_2.text: The Concierge has fallen asleep on the counter. The master key hangs from his neck on a thin ribbon. The reception bell waits, barely touching his hand.
event.concierge_2.title: The master key
event.confession_booth.ra: You say too much. You leave lighter... and somewhere in a ledger, something weighs a little more.
event.confession_booth.rb: As you walk away you hear your own voice confessing on the other side.
event.confession_booth.rh: “Part of it can be erased,” it whispers. “But you have to want it.” The debt loosens.
event.confession_booth.text: A confessional between two tables. On the other side someone breathes slowly and waits for you to speak first.
event.confession_booth.title: The confessional
event.cook_1.ra: It’s hot and tastes of something you remember without having lived it. You feel better; the bill notices too.
event.cook_1.rb: He shrugs. “More for the Child,” he says, and sets aside a plate no one comes to collect.
event.cook_1.text: In the kitchen a man in a stained apron stirs an enormous pot. “Eat,” says the Cook, “everything gets used here.” You don’t know what the soup is made of.
event.cook_1.title: Soup of the day
event.cook_2.b: Leave him a memory of yours
event.cook_2.ra: It smells of rain and of a kitchen that isn’t this one. For a moment you understand how to improve your hands. The memory evaporates, and the label with it.
event.cook_2.rb: You pick one of your memories and he puts it in an empty jar. “Fair price,” he says, counting out some coins. You don’t miss a thing. That’s the strange part.
event.cook_2.text: The pantry has shelves of labeled jars: a birthday, a farewell, an ordinary Monday. “Memories in preserve,” the Cook explains. “My brother takes what’s left over.”
event.cook_2.title: The jars
event.cook_3.ra: The Vendor takes it without thanking you and pays you. “My brother cooks well,” he says. “It’s the only thing he doesn’t charge for.” He no longer looks at you with indifference.
event.cook_3.rb: Inside is a one-line note and a card you don’t remember seeing. The Cook knows before you leave the pantry.
event.cook_3.text: The Cook hands you a box tied with string. “For my brother,” he says. “The one who sells what I keep. Don’t open it.”
event.cook_3.title: An errand for the Vendor
event.cracked_clock.ra: Something creaks inside. The clock stays in your hand, stopped, and you no longer know what time it is.
event.cracked_clock.rb: It is safer not to touch time here. You find a few coins under the pendulum.
event.cracked_clock.text: A wall clock always reads 3:33. If you stare at it, the second hand trembles, as if asking for something.
event.cracked_clock.title: The stopped clock
event.dealer_offer.ra: The ink is warm. The paper folds itself inside your coat. You feel light, and watched.
event.dealer_offer.rb: He takes the contract back without pressing. “The offer expires.” He leaves you a few coins for the trouble. That is worse.
event.dealer_offer.text: The Dealer slides a contract across the table. “One signature and that debt disappears.” The small print moves.
event.dealer_offer.title: The offer
event.dealer_question.ra: He writes something down. “How curious. Nobody remembers.” He looks at you as if you had just lied to a mirror.
event.dealer_question.rb: “Neither do I,” he admits, and for the first time the deck stops. You ask his name. He is silent. He has none.
event.dealer_question.rh: “Fifty-two cards,” he says, unsurprised. “Four suits, thirteen each, Ace to King. And one that isn’t there.” He smiles.
event.dealer_question.text: “Do you remember how you got here?” asks the Dealer, shuffling without looking. “Before the first hand.”
event.dealer_question.title: A question
event.dealer_tea.ra: Warm, sweet, far too familiar. Inside the cup, engraved, your name. You feel better anyway.
event.dealer_tea.rb: He withdraws the cup, unoffended. “Whenever you like.” You both know it isn’t politeness.
event.dealer_tea.text: The Dealer pours tea into two identical cups. “Rest a little. The house is paying.” The steam draws a number.
event.dealer_tea.title: The Dealer’s tea
event.debt_collector.ra: He counts the bills twice and writes something down. “A pleasure.”
event.debt_collector.rb: “I shall note it with interest.” He leaves without a sound. The cold stays.
event.debt_collector.text: A man in a grey suit waits with a receipt. “Your debt, sir. It bears your signature.” You don’t remember signing.
event.debt_collector.title: The collector
event.dice_pit.ra: The dice roll and stop. The voice already knew the result.
event.dice_pit.rb: The voice clicks its tongue. “Another time.” You hear it laughing below.
event.dice_pit.text: A sand pit with bone dice. A bodiless voice asks: “Heads or tails?” The dice have neither.
event.dice_pit.title: The dice pit
event.drowned_pier.ra: He grips you. Heavy, freezing, he whispers his payment: someone sank him over a debt that was yours. He leaves you a handful of salt.
event.drowned_pier.rb: The knocking follows behind you, always at the same distance.
event.drowned_pier.text: A wooden pier with no water. Below, a man soaked to the bone knocks on the floor with his knuckles, very slowly.
event.drowned_pier.title: The dry pier
event.first_chip.ra: It weighs more than it looks. Something in a book you cannot see has just been written down.
event.first_chip.rb: The chip vanishes into the dark. The Dealer nods, as if he had expected it.
event.first_chip.text: A black chip rolls to your feet. The Dealer smiles without moving his mouth: “It’s yours. It always was.”
event.first_chip.title: The black chip
event.girl_1.ra: The coin spins far too long. It lands, or it doesn’t; she has already looked away.
event.girl_1.rb: “How dull,” she says, pocketing the coin. She follows you with her good eye until you are gone.
event.girl_1.text: A girl with one eye sewn shut with red thread spins a coin. “Heads or tails. You choose. I watch.”
event.girl_1.title: The Girl with the Stitched Eye
event.girl_2.ra: You thank her. You accept her advice and her money; both turn out false, though useful.
event.girl_2.rb: She smiles crookedly. “Clever.” You learn her tell: she lies when she looks at the floor.
event.girl_2.text: “I’m warning you: the House doesn’t lie,” says the girl with the stitched eye. She says it staring at the floor. It is the kind of sentence said while lying.
event.girl_2.title: What the girl says
event.girl_3.ra: You put it in and see more: the cards, the room, something behind the room. She keeps the thread.
event.girl_3.rb: “Another time, then.” She closes her hand, and the eye, if it was an eye, is gone.
event.girl_3.text: The girl offers a glass eye on her open palm. “This one sees more. It costs more, too.” The red thread has come loose a little.
event.girl_3.title: The red thread
event.kitchen_fire.ra: You pick one with your signature and toss it in. It burns blue. The debt lightens… and something inside you does too.
event.kitchen_fire.rb: You stir slowly. For a moment the broth looks like your face. You ladle some out; it does you good, and the house charges for it.
event.kitchen_fire.text: Old papers burn beneath the big pot: IOUs, receipts, promises. The Cook is away. The fire looks at you hungrily.
event.kitchen_fire.title: The stove
event.merchant_memory.ra: You uncork it and suddenly you play one hand better. You don’t know why.
event.merchant_memory.rb: “Whenever you like.” He is slightly offended. He is the only merchant who never turns his back.
event.merchant_memory.text: The Peddler sells memories in jars. “This one smells like your first casino. That one, like your last hand.”
event.merchant_memory.title: A memory for sale
event.mirror_hall.ra: It is warm, like a hand. Your reflection smiles half a second before you do.
event.mirror_hall.rb: You count the steps to the exit. Nobody follows you. Nobody, except one.
event.mirror_hall.rh: The reflection nods. For the first time you feel that someone on that side plays in your favor.
event.mirror_hall.text: Every mirror returns your gesture a second late. The last one does not follow you: it watches you.
event.mirror_hall.title: The hall of mirrors
event.moon_window.ra: The air smells of wax. You know something you didn’t: the Man in the Chair cannot bear this light.
event.moon_window.rb: You close it slowly. On the other side of the glass something knocks twice, politely.
event.moon_window.text: A wall-less window shows an enormous moon. In the rest of the casino it is daytime.
event.moon_window.title: The window
event.nun_1.ra: You talk for what feels like a whole night. You leave lighter… and with a slightly longer bill. She notes something on the beads of her rosary.
event.nun_1.rb: She nods slowly. “Silence is also a debt,” she says, and lights a candle without asking you for anything.
event.nun_1.text: A nun in a black veil makes room for you in the confessional. “Tell me what you owe,” says the Sister. “Everything is said here, even if no one listens.”
event.nun_1.title: The veil
event.nun_2.ra: “He had a debt and I offered him water. He accepted. It’s paid, though he doesn’t believe it.” At last you understand what happened to the Drowned Man.
event.nun_2.rb: You pray without words. You feel the weight of a hand that isn’t there. You leave with less fear and damp shoes.
event.nun_2.rh: The Sister crosses herself. “I know it. He confessed it once, long ago, before the first hand.” She presses her lips together: she won’t tell you. But now you know there was a name.
event.nun_2.text: “I baptized one for too long,” the Sister murmurs, looking at the font. “Now he lives downstairs and never dries.” The candles lean toward the floor.
event.nun_2.title: The baptism
event.nun_3.ra: You say words you don’t remember learning. She weeps without a sound and, rising, hands you something you don’t remember losing either.
event.nun_3.rb: You walk away with her murmur behind you. In the collection box there are a few coins; you can’t tell whether they’re yours or hers.
event.nun_3.text: This time it is the Sister who kneels. “I confessed first,” she says. “And I gave him absolution before he had anything to be forgiven.”
event.nun_3.title: The last confession
event.nurse_1.ra: It doesn’t hurt. She closes wounds you didn’t know you had and leaves others unopened. “There,” she says. “Now, to bed.” You don’t stay.
event.nurse_1.rb: She looks at you for a long moment. “As you wish.” She puts the needle on a tray with a dozen more. It’s not the first time someone has said no.
event.nurse_1.text: A nurse in a green mask pulls back a curtain. “Sit down, dear. You look awful. No one is cured here, but everyone gets a little better.” She holds a threaded needle.
event.nurse_1.title: The infirmary
event.nurse_2.ra: “She saw what lies behind the deck. The Dealer asked me politely.” You understand why the Girl lies: it’s the one thing they didn’t sew shut.
event.nurse_2.rb: The black thread tangles around your fingers and one of your cards ends up marked with a stitch. It looks as if it was always that way.
event.nurse_2.text: On the tray lie needles, black thread and a glass eye. “It’s the Girl’s,” says the Nurse. “I sewed hers shut so she’d stop seeing. Now she asks me to do it again every night.”
event.nurse_2.title: The tray
event.nurse_3.ra: You go down the corridor slowly. He talks about when the house was one salon and one table. “I stayed to wait for the others,” he repeats. And the others came.
event.nurse_3.rb: You swap the label. He doesn’t protest; neither does the Nurse. “If he stands, we’ll see who sits,” she finally says. There is something they no longer charge you for.
event.nurse_3.text: The Man in the Chair waits in the infirmary corridor. A syringe rests in his lap. “My dose,” he murmurs. “So I don’t stand up.” The Nurse watches you from the doorway.
event.nurse_3.title: The dose
event.old_photograph.ra: Behind it there are names. Many. None repeats... except yours.
event.old_photograph.rb: You leave it. You still feel watched, but with a certain kindness. Almost.
event.old_photograph.text: A group photo hangs on the wall: players around this table, from every era. In the back row, your face.
event.old_photograph.title: The photograph
event.phone_call.ra: A breath and, beneath it, a murmur of distant applause. “Are you still there?” says someone who isn’t in the room. “We are.”
event.phone_call.rb: The phone falls silent the moment you touch it. As you hang up, a collective sigh is heard.
event.phone_call.text: A bakelite phone rings in the middle of the table. It’s for you. It’s always for you, from the second time on.
event.phone_call.title: The telephone
event.pianist_1.ra: It lasts as long as it lasts. You feel light, almost forgiven. You leave a coin in his tailcoat pocket.
event.pianist_1.rb: “It’s the only one I know.” He plays it again, just as perfect. When it ends he holds out an empty cuff: inside are some coins you don’t remember leaving.
event.pianist_1.rh: “I left them as payment,” he says. “The Dealer wanted them for his first deck. Now the Archivist keeps them in a drawer that never opens.” And he goes on playing.
event.pianist_1.text: A pianist with empty cuffs plays the chapel organ. There are no hands in his sleeves, yet the music sounds. “It’s the only piece I remember,” he says without turning.
event.pianist_1.title: The organist
event.pianist_2.ra: You spin until the floor forgets you. You feel better, and worse. She whispers: “Thank you for not letting go.”
event.pianist_2.rb: You look at each other without a word. Her dress sways without wind. The Pianist plays more softly, as if apologizing.
event.pianist_2.text: The Woman in Red dances alone among the pews to the rhythm of the organ. If the Pianist stopped, what would become of her? She offers you a gloved hand.
event.pianist_2.title: The dance
event.prompter_1.ra: You say “good evening” and cough. The audience that isn’t there applauds. Someone leaves coins in the box; the Prompter pushes them toward you without looking.
event.prompter_1.rb: The silence does you good. He sighs like someone who’s lost his place and mutters a line to the void. For a moment, no one tells you what to say.
event.prompter_1.rh: “The Dummy? I prompt him, from here. But the box has no bottom: I don’t even know where my own lines come from.” You look inside: it’s true, there’s only more darkness.
event.prompter_1.text: Beneath the stage, a booth shaped like a shell. Inside, a man in thin glasses whispers your line before you think it: “Say ‘good evening’, then cough.” It is the Prompter.
event.prompter_1.title: The prompt box
event.prompter_2.ra: You squint until you can read it: “The Dealer has a part here too.” You understand that everyone in the house plays a role… and that someone casts them.
event.prompter_2.rb: The page crumbles in your hand like cold ash. The Prompter doesn’t protest: “Someone had to tear it out sooner or later.” You breathe easier.
event.prompter_2.text: The Prompter shows you the bound script. Your name appears on every page. On the last, the writing shrinks and vanishes: “Here the audience improvises,” he says.
event.prompter_2.title: Act three
event.puppet_1.ra: It repeats whole sentences: the same ones the Dealer said to those before you. You notice a pause before each, as if someone were prompting from behind.
event.puppet_1.rb: It falls limp with a knock of wood. In its pocket are some coins and an unsigned note: “Keep going without looking back.”
event.puppet_1.text: A ventriloquist’s dummy sits on an empty chair. With no one moving it, its jaw drops: “Welcome,” it says in a voice you’ve heard before. “We were expecting you.”
event.puppet_1.title: The dummy
event.puppet_2.ra: You say exactly what was written and everything goes well, too well. The bill lightens. Somewhere, the Dealer seems to smile.
event.puppet_2.rb: You say a line that wasn’t there. The Dummy is left with its mouth open. For an instant, the whole house has to improvise.
event.puppet_2.text: The Dummy speaks again. This time it doesn’t repeat the Dealer: it reads your own lines, before you say them. “Page thirty,” it announces. “This is where you hesitate.”
event.puppet_2.title: The script
event.room_13.ra: Inside, the Child waits with the cards in its hands. “Did you lose again?”
event.room_13.rb: You shut it. The door dissolves into the wall as if it had never been there.
event.room_13.text: At the end of the corridor stands a door that wasn’t there: 13. Behind it, the sound of a child shuffling, very slowly.
event.room_13.title: Room 13
event.secret_bone_door.ra: The bone key was in your pocket all along. Behind the door: a room with no exit and air that smells like real air.
event.secret_bone_door.rb: You find a few coins by the door. The door waits.
event.secret_bone_door.text: A door made of small, polished bones. It has a lock. And it has your key, though you haven’t seen it yet.
event.secret_bone_door.title: The bone door
event.secret_stage.ra: From your seat you see a table, a deck and an empty chair. You understand you are not the only one playing here. Nor the only one watching.
event.secret_stage.rb: You prefer to remain standing. A short rest, and slightly lighter air.
event.secret_stage.text: A casino stage with empty seats. Each one bears a name plate. One bears yours. Another, the Dealer’s: it is blank.
event.secret_stage.title: The empty stage
event.secret_watcher.ra: It looks at you. You look at it. And for a moment you feel that someone else is watching you both, from outside the room.
event.secret_watcher.rb: You look down. The eye on the ceiling seems relieved, as if it feared being looked at.
event.secret_watcher.text: A room without doors with an eye painted on the ceiling. Nobody painted it. It blinks when you blink.
event.secret_watcher.title: The one who watches
event.signed_receipt.ra: It is a list of games. All lost. All yours.
event.signed_receipt.rb: You tear it to pieces. When you close your fist it is whole again in your pocket, but lighter.
event.signed_receipt.text: A folded receipt falls from your pocket. It has your handwriting, an amount you don’t understand, and tomorrow’s date.
event.signed_receipt.title: The signed receipt
event.staff_room.ra: Each of them covers a shift for a guest who never left. You grasp something uncomfortable: every one of them played before. Every one.
event.staff_room.rb: You run a finger over your name and it vanishes. It reappears on the other side of the room. At least there are some forgotten coins in a locker.
event.staff_room.text: A room with lockers and a shift board: Dealer, Archivist, Vendor, Cook, Nurse, Sister, Pianist… There’s a slot with your name on the last shift of the night.
event.staff_room.title: The staff room
event.theatre_seats.ra: You bow. The applause multiplies, grows deafening… and stops dead. On stage lies something for you: a purse of coins tied with ribbon.
event.theatre_seats.rb: You tiptoe out. The coats don’t move. Only when you close the door do you hear behind you a sigh of disappointment, from a thousand mouths.
event.theatre_seats.text: The house is full of coats and hats on seats with no one inside them. When you enter, all the coats turn toward you at once. A single, slow clap is heard.
event.theatre_seats.title: The stalls
event.usher_1.ra: You sink into the velvet. You rest as you couldn’t remember being able to. The show begins and no one walks on stage… but they charge admission on the way out.
event.usher_1.rb: “As you wish.” She switches off the beam and stands beside you, motionless. A coin drops to the floor; you don’t know who left it.
event.usher_1.text: A woman in a pillbox cap shines a flashlight at your shoes. “This way, please. Row thirteen, seat thirteen. We were expecting you.” The seat is warm.
event.usher_1.title: Your seat
event.usher_2.ra: On number thirteen lie a coat in your size and a hat with your initials. Every other name is crossed out. Yours isn’t. You feel watched, and not only by her.
event.usher_2.rb: The darkness is total. She laughs softly. “Now that is a show.” Among the seats you feel for forgotten coins and leave in a hurry.
event.usher_2.text: The Usher sweeps her flashlight along the rows. On every seat, a folded coat, a hat, a cane. “No one leaves,” she whispers. “They leave their things and stay. Look at number thirteen.”
event.usher_2.title: The beam of light
event.wall_notes.ra: There’s more: bets, debts, a couple of jokes. Among the scribbles, some forgotten money in a crack.
event.wall_notes.rb: They say whoever reads it all stays to live here. You’d rather not find out.
event.wall_notes.text: Someone has written on the wall in chalk, in charcoal, in blood: “The Nurse stitched the eye.” “The Cook keeps the memories.” “The Vendor sells them.” “The Sister knows the name.” “The Pianist paid with his hands.” Below, smaller: “No one remembers who writes this.”
event.wall_notes.title: Notes on the wall
event.watcher_1.ra: You see yourself from above, waiting. You watch your lips move in this very sentence. The Watchman jots something down and slides you a few coins: “For the trouble.”
event.watcher_1.rb: You press a button and the picture jumps to an empty room, then another, then to a room with no number. The Watchman looks at you for the first time: “That shouldn’t come up.”
event.watcher_1.rh: He doesn’t answer. But his gaze drops for a second to a corner of the wall where no screen covers the plaster. “There’s a gap there,” he admits, very quietly. “I don’t know what’s in it. No one can see.”
event.watcher_1.text: A wall of green and blue screens: the Salon, the Corridor, the Chapel, the Kitchens… On one, your own back. A man in a cap doesn’t look away: “Sit down. Don’t talk. I’ll note it down.”
event.watcher_1.title: The monitors
event.watcher_2.ra: For a few seconds, no one sees you. It is a silence that almost hurts. You learn where it begins and where it ends, and that from here the house seems less watchful.
event.watcher_2.rb: You hold your hands over your face. A screen flickers and stops following you. The Watchman pretends to have seen nothing. You feel a little lighter.
event.watcher_2.text: The Watchman points to a corner of the ceiling. “That camera faces the wall. Always. Someone turned it years ago.” Beneath it, a square of wall with no screen, no dust, no shadow.
event.watcher_2.title: The blind spot
event.wet_footprints.ra: Behind the door there is an empty table and a handful of damp chips. Nobody claims them.
event.wet_footprints.rb: You prefer not to know. The floor, however, keeps getting wet behind you.
event.wet_footprints.text: Wet, bare footprints cross the carpet and disappear under a door. Someone has just passed.
event.wet_footprints.title: Wet footprints
event.woman_dress.ra: The card grows warm. Turned over, it shows someone who wept a great deal and regrets nothing.
event.woman_dress.rb: She pockets the card without insisting. You know she will offer it again.
event.woman_dress.text: A woman in a dark red dress holds out a card face down. “Four times as much of everything,” she says. “Debts included.”
event.woman_dress.title: The Woman in Red
fx.abandoned: You left the room half-finished. The house took something.
fx.collapse: Your mind cracks: you lose Health and regain some Sanity.
fx.revive_candle: The short candle lights you again.
fx.revive_life: An extra life drags you back from death.
help.goal: Reach the point TARGET before you run out of plays. If you don’t, the house collects.
help.score: Each play scores CHIPS × MULT. The hand (pair, three of a kind, straight…) sets the base; every card and combo adds more. Always check the cost before playing. Each card adds chips by its value: Ace 11, face cards (J, Q, K) 10, the rest their number.
help.stakes: Staking multiplies the play but costs Health, Sanity, Money or Debt. Some rules forbid it.
help.tips: Discard weak cards, keep one in the Pocket for the perfect play, and watch your Sanity: when it drops, the screen distorts, and at 0 you collapse (+25 Sanity, −20 Health).
help.title: Quick guide
hint.boss: Each wing has a Guardian with rules of its own that change the game. Read them before you play: defeating it brings you closer to the end.
hint.event: Here you choose between two options: REJECT (← or A) or ACCEPT (→ or D). What changes —Health, Sanity, Money or Debt— you will see afterwards. At 0 Health you die, with low Sanity the house distorts, and Debt grows with interest.
hint.map: Tap a room to see what it is and tap it again to enter.
hint.merchant: Everything here is bought with Money. And money is lent too: loans add Debt, and Debt grows with interest after every room.
hint.rest: A breather: choose just one thing. Sleeping restores Health, breathing restores Sanity, paying lowers Debt and studying levels up a hand.
howto.s1.t:
You descend through the house room by room. On each floor you choose your path on the map: you play card tables, decide in events and, sometimes, stake something in the shotgun duel. Each wing ends with a Guardian; after that come the Dealer, his last hand and The Door.
Dying is not the end: you keep memories and knowledge, and you go down again.
howto.s2.t:
Each room is a node. Tap one to see what it is and tap it again (or press ENTER) to go in. You can only move to rooms connected to yours.
There are card tables, events, the Vendor, rests, the shotgun (a duel where you stake something of yours), a secret bone door and the Guardian.
howto.s3.t:
• Health: at 0 you die. An extra candle lifts you back up once, with 40% Health.
• Sanity: it drops with cards, stakes and events. When low, the screen distorts and whispers appear; at 0 you collapse: you regain 25 Sanity but lose 20 Health.
• Money: buys things at the shop and pays off debt.
• Debt: it grows with loans and stakes, and 1.4% interest is added after every room. With a lot of debt, the House raises the table targets by 5% for every 100 over 200 (up to 25%).
• Shield: absorbs the Health cost of cards.
howto.s4.t:
Pick 1 to 5 cards from your hand and play: the hand (pair, three of a kind, straight…) gives chips × multiplier, and each card and combo adds more. Reach the target before you run out of plays; if you don’t, you pay with Health, Sanity and Debt.
You can discard, keep a card in the Pocket or stake (it multiplies the play, but it costs). Each opponent brings a rule of its own, shown on the table. Always check the cost before playing.
howto.s5.t: They are two-option decisions: REJECT (← or A) or ACCEPT (→ or D); on a phone, swipe. Sometimes a third, hidden option (H) appears, depending on what you know or carry. What your decision changes is shown afterwards, and some tools let you redo it.
howto.s6.t:
You stake something of yours (Money, Sanity, Debt or a card). The shotgun has 6 chambers, some loaded. The opponent announces how many bullets there are… and may lie.
On your turn you can shoot the opponent (if the chamber is loaded, it loses a mark; if not, the turn passes), tempt the Table (if it is empty you keep your turn; if not, you lose a mark) or listen (it costs Sanity and is not always right). Whoever leaves the other with no marks wins.
howto.s7.t:
The Vendor sells items, tools and cards for Money, and he also lends: loans add Debt.
At a rest you choose just one thing: sleep (Health), breathe (Sanity), pay debt or study a hand to level it up.
howto.s8.t:
When you die you see your CURRENT DEBT (part of it carries over to your next descent) and your MEMORIES KEPT: permanent perks earned by doing certain things. What you discover is saved as knowledge and opens hidden options and doors.
There are 6 endings; The Door asks for different things for each one.
howto.s9.t:
Some cards cost you Health when they score (Blood, Hunger…). The SHIELD is spent first: each point absorbs one point of that Health.
• Keys and some special cards and items give it.
• It shows next to your plays and lasts the whole round.
• It does not stop stakes or opponent effects.
howto.title: How to play
hud.debt.tip: What you owe the house: it grows with loans, bets and interest. When high, targets rise (up to +25%). In return, some cards and jokers turn it into points. Pay it off at rests.
hud.deck.tip: See all your cards, special ones highlighted. Sort them by suit, rank, special or newest.
hud.health.tip: Your life. At 0 you die. Blood cards, Health bets and lost rounds spend it; you recover it by sleeping at a rest or with bandages from the shop.
hud.lives.tip: Each candle is a life. You start with one; if your Health hits 0 and you have another, it burns out and you return with 40% Health.
hud.money.tip: Use it to buy in the shop (jokers, items, cards, bandages…) and to pay off Debt at a rest. You earn it by winning rounds and duels.
hud.sanity.tip: Your mind. It drains when you listen in a duel and from bets, cursed cards and events. When low the screen distorts; at 0 you collapse (−20 Health, +25 Sanity). Breathe at a rest to recover it.
intro.3: We have to finish a game.
intro.6: Sit down. I’ll show you how we play here.

know.k_chair_founder.name: The founder
know.k_chair_founder.text: The Man in the Chair founded the house and never got up.
know.k_child_self.name: The child is you
know.k_child_self.text: The child in the birthday dress was you. Its “blind eyes” rule no longer blinds you.
know.k_concierge_keys.name: The Concierge’s ring
know.k_concierge_keys.text: The Concierge has a key for every door in the house but one: the way out. Someone else keeps that.
know.k_cook_jars.name: The jars
know.k_cook_jars.text: The Cook preserves memories in jars and the Vendor sells them. You know where his hunger comes from: he no longer demands extra of you.
know.k_dealer_deck.name: The Dealer’s deck
know.k_dealer_deck.text: The Dealer always deals from the bottom. His deck has no king.
know.k_dealer_ledger.name: The Dealer’s ledger
know.k_dealer_ledger.text: In his ledger every line is a game. The last one is missing.
know.k_dealer_no_name.name: The Dealer has no name
know.k_dealer_no_name.text: Nobody remembers the Dealer’s name. Neither does he.
know.k_door_same.name: All the doors are the same
know.k_door_same.text: Every door leads to the same room. You need to know this to see the truth.
know.k_drowned_paid.name: The Drowned Man has paid
know.k_drowned_paid.text: The Drowned Man paid his debt in water. His “drowning” rule no longer sinks you.
know.k_girl_lies.name: What the girl lies about
know.k_girl_lies.text: The girl with the stitched eye lies when she tells the truth. Her “no repeats” rule no longer binds you.
know.k_moon.name: The window’s moon
know.k_moon.text: The window’s moon is a spotlight. Without its cold, the Man in the Chair loses his rule.
know.k_nun_name.name: The Dealer’s name
know.k_nun_name.text: The Sister knows what the Dealer was called and won’t say. But you know he once had a name. Her punishment for repeating plays no longer reaches you.
know.k_nurse_eye.name: The stitched eye
know.k_nurse_eye.text: The Nurse stitched the Girl’s eye because it saw too much. You know what her lies hide, and Eyes work for you again against the Nurse.
know.k_pianist_hands.name: The Pianist’s hands
know.k_pianist_hands.text: The Pianist paid with his hands for the house’s first deck. The Archivist keeps them in a drawer that never opens.
know.k_players.name: The players
know.k_prompter_box.name: The Prompter’s box
know.k_prompter_box.text: The box has no bottom: the Prompter writes over what you’ve already said. You know where he whispers from, and his Memory no longer punishes you for repeating plays.
know.k_puppet_script.name: The script
know.k_puppet_script.text: The Dummy repeats the Dealer’s script. Everything said here is written down; what’s missing is by whom.
know.k_reflection.name: Your reflection
know.k_reflection.text: In the mirror, you are not the one who moves first.
know.k_room13.name: Room 13
know.k_room13.text: There is a room that appears on no floor plan.
know.k_usher_seat.name: Seat 13
know.k_usher_seat.text: Every seat in the house was paid for by someone who never left. Number 13 is yours, and it is warm.
know.k_watcher.name: Someone is watching

legal.privacy.s1.t:
The game stores your save and your settings (language, volume, accessibility) in your browser’s local storage. This data stays on your device: the game does not send it to any server.
You can erase it with RESET PROGRESS in the menu or from your browser settings. If you erase it, you lose your save.
legal.privacy.s2.t: The game includes no advertising or analytics, uses no cookies and loads no resources from other sites. It does not collect personal data.
legal.privacy.s3.t: Like any website, the hosting where the game is published (currently GitHub Pages) may log technical data about visits, such as the IP address, under its own terms. The game does not receive that data.
legal.privacy.s4.t:
THE HOUSE ALWAYS WATCHES is a work of horror fiction: the characters, places and events are imaginary.
The money, chips, bets and debts in the game are fictional: they have no real value, they cannot be bought or exchanged for real money, and the game is not a gambling service.
It includes flicker and shaking effects, and visual distortion when Sanity drops. You can reduce them in SETTINGS → Reduce effects. If you have photosensitive epilepsy or other discomfort, talk to a professional before playing.

tut.d0: The shotgun: six chambers, some loaded. The foe announces how many bullets there are… and may lie.
tut.d1: Shoot the foe if you think the chamber is loaded. Listening costs Sanity and is not always right.
tut.d2: Tempting the Table is safe if the chamber is empty: you keep your turn. If it is loaded, you lose a mark.
tut.done: “Good. The house knows how you play now.”
tut.r1: Tap cards to pick them (up to 5) and press PLAY. Pairs score more: try the two 8s.
tut.r2: Each suit has its own effect. Eyes give chips and reveal cards from the deck. Three Eyes together form THE GAZE.
tut.r3: Blood gives multiplier but costs Health. Always check what a play costs before you make it.
tut.r4: You can DISCARD bad cards or keep one in the POCKET. Staking multiplies a play… but the house collects.
tut.r5: Reach the target before you run out of plays. If you don’t, you pay.
tut.r6: You know the basics now: carry on at your own pace. Rivals and rooms will bring new rules.
